The component html will be the html that is used to render the component. This will be used in the Angular Template for the component, so is the equivalent of what would be in the html template for an AngularJS directive

An example is setting the address fields on change in an address component:

FIELD WATCH FUNCTION


The watch function allows operations to happen when the field changes. This is typically used for functionality that allows the behaviour of the component to take place, like setting fields within the component, rather than the OnFieldChange rule functionality

An example is setting the address fields on change in an address component:
    

EXAMPLE:


    function (newValue, oldValue) {

        var ctrlName = scope.fieldName;
        ...
    }

COMPONENT LIBRARY DOCUMENTS


The component library documents will have the common code like variables and functions which would be used in custom component. This document will also have a systemHeader.systemType of "component", because this is a component that contains functions and variables, rather than a GUI component.

These are selected from the list of available common components documents.

components.html:
COMPONENT LOAD FUNCTION


The component load function will be the function that is called on load of the component. This will be the equivalent of what would be put in the link function of a directive if developing a component as a plain directive.

An example is setting the onload function in importing CSV files.


EXAMPLE:


    function () {
      var contents = e.target.result;

      $scope.$apply(function () {
        var csvArray = baby.parse(contents.trim()).data;
        var hasHeader = utilCSV.validateColumnHeader(csvArray, labels);
        var startRow = 0;
          if (hasHeader)
            startRow = 1;

            for (var i = startRow; i < csvArray.length; i++) {
            var row = csvArray[i];
            var object = {};
              for (var j = 0; j < row.length; j++) {
                object[j + ''] = row[j];
              }

              $scope.items.push(object);
            }
            });

      };

CLEANUP FUNCTION


The cleanup function will perform any cleanup needed on destroy of the component. This will be the equivalent of what would be put in the destroy function of a directive if developing a component as a plain directive.

An example is cleaning up the Google Places data in an address component:

EXAMPLE:


    GooglePlacesService.cleanup(autocomplete);

components.html:
SERVER PREPROCESSOR FUNCTION


This will be called in a server-side preprocessor for custom components. Preprocessors are called from MongoPreProcessor.js.

An example is converting a checkbox value to boolean:

EXAMPLE:


    function verifyInput(field, document){
        var value;

        if(!!document[field.name] && _.isString(document[field.name])){
           if(document[field.name] === "true" || document[field.name] === "false" ){
              value = JSON.parse(document[field.name]);
           }else{
              ...
              logger.error("Preprocessing Failure : " + errMsg);
              return null;
           }

         return value;

        }

RESTFUL WEBSERVICE FUNCTIONS:


This will be called in a server-side for custom components through a restful web service. Functions are called from ComponentFunctionController.js.

An example is getting AVL event data:

EXAMPLE:

{
  getAvlEvent : function(args) {
      var deferred = q.defer();
      var query = {'features.properties.imei': args[0]}
      DataService.findAll(query, req.user.documentId)
      .then(function successFunc(docs) {
           deferred.resolve(docs);
      }, function errorFunc(err) {
           deferred.reject(err);
     });
     return deferred.promise;
  }
}

These are selected from the list of available common external library documents.
